_doc: Ask an AI settings for topic notes and the Upload page's practice-set picker. Edit this file to change the wording, add a mode, or switch assistants — no code changes needed. Placeholders are filled from the open topic note (never the student's name, school or grades): {subject} (e.g. Biology), {level} (HL or SL), {topic} (code, title and theme), {understandings} (key-idea cues with statement codes), {keyterms} (term: short definition), {wrong_questions} (stems of unresolved misses on this topic's linked quiz items; our own question text only, no markschemes), {subjectid} (the raw subject id, e.g. biology-hl — for prompts that must emit a subject id the app understands), {topickey} (the short topic key used by uploaded banks, e.g. a1-1; callers must set note.topicKey — notes.js does, and the Upload picker passes the manifest entry's file basename). subjectNames (optional) maps a subject id to a proper course name for {subject}; the level still comes from a -hl/-sl suffix or hlOnly. Mode templates may use only these placeholders. default_ai must match an assistants[].id. After editing, run ./dev.sh test (or node --test tests/js/ai-prompt.test.js).
preamble: You are an experienced IB {subject} {level} teacher. The student is in DP1 (first year of the Diploma Programme) and will sit first exams in May 2028. Stay on the current IB {subject} {level} syllabus for {topic}. If you are unsure, say so. Do not present your questions or marking notes as real IB exam questions, markschemes or exam predictions. Do not ask for or use any personal information about the student.

modes.label: Explain, then check my understanding
Quiz me one question at a time
Data-response in an unfamiliar scenario
Help with my wrong answers
Write a practice set to import
modes.template:
Write a practice quiz I can import into my revision app for {topic} (IB {subject} {level}, DP1). Output ONLY the raw JSON — no markdown code fences (no ```), no explanation before or after. Write original questions yourself; never copy IB past-paper questions or markschemes. Do not present them as real IB exam questions or predictions.

Fill this EXACT JSON shape:
{
  "subject": "{subjectid}",
  "topic": "{topickey}",
  "topicLabel": "a short human-readable name for {topic}",
  "items": [
    {"id": "p01", "format": "mcq", "topic": "{topickey}",
     "stem": "question text", "choices": ["option A", "option B", "option C", "option D"],
     "answer": 1,
     "note": "why the answer is right AND the trap people fall into"},
    {"id": "p02", "format": "written", "topic": "{topickey}", "marks": 3,
     "stem": "question text needing 2-4 sentences or a calculation",
     "markscheme": ["marking point (1 mark)", "marking point (1 mark)", "marking point (1 mark)"],
     "tactic": "how to attack this question type"}
  ]
}

Rules:
- 8 questions total: 5 MCQ (ids p01–p05), 3 written (ids p06–p08).
- Use exactly "subject": "{subjectid}" and exactly "topic": "{topickey}" — in the bank and repeated in every item.
- "answer" is the 0-based index into "choices" (first option = 0).
- MCQ distractors must be plausible — real misconceptions, not joke answers.
- Written markschemes: one short marking point per mark, like a real markscheme.
